source_text: Ceterum si quae audent interserere se aetati apostolicae, ut ideo videantur ab apostolis traditae quia sub apostolis fuerunt, possumus dicere: Edant ergo origines ecclesiarum suarum, evolvant ordinem episcoporum suorum, ita per successionem ab initio decurrentem, ut primus ille episcopus aliquem ex apostolis vel apostolicis viris, qui tamen cum apostolis perseveravit, habuerit auctorem et antecessorem. Hoc enim modo ecclesiae apostolicae census suos deferunt, sicut Smyrnaeorum ecclesia Polycarpum ab Ioanne collocatum refert, sicut Romanorum Clementem a Petro ordinatum itidem. Perinde utique et ceterae exhibent quos ab apostolis in episcopatum constitutos apostolici seminis traduces habeant. Confingant tale aliquid haeretici. Quid enim illis post blasphemiam inlicitum est? Sed etsi confinxerint, nihil promovebunt. Ipsa enim doctrina eorum cum apostolica comparata ex diversitate et contrarietate sua pronuntiabit neque apostoli alicuius auctoris esse neque apostolici, quia sicut apostoli non diversa inter se docuissent, ita et apostolici non contraria apostolis edidissent. Nisi illi qui ab apostolis didicerunt aliter praedicaverunt. Ad hanc itaque formam probabuntur ab illis ecclesiis, quae licet nullum ex apostolis vel apostolicis auctorem suum proferant, ut multo posteriores, quae denique cottidie instituuntur, tamen in eadem fide conspirantes non minus apostolicae deputantur pro consanguinitate doctrinae. Ita omnes haereses ad utramque formam a nostris ecclesiis provocatae probent se quaqua putant apostolicas. Sed adeo nec sunt nec probare possunt quod non sunt, nec recipiuntur in pacem et communicationem ab ecclesiis quoquo modo apostolicis, scilicet ob diversitatem sacramenti nullo modo apostolicae.
thought_title: Apostolic succession as the test of true churches
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that heretics cannot claim apostolic origin, and now proposes that any church claiming apostolic descent must produce the succession of its bishops from an apostle or apostolic man.
pass_a_gloss: But if any dare to insert themselves into the apostolic age, so that they may seem to have been handed down by the apostles because they existed under the apostles, we can say: Let them then produce the origins of their churches, let them unroll the order of their bishops, running down from the beginning by succession in such a way that that first bishop had as his author and predecessor some one of the apostles or apostolic men, who nevertheless persevered with the apostles. For in this way the apostolic churches present their records, just as the church of the Smyrnaeans reports that Polycarp was placed by John, just as the church of the Romans reports that Clement was ordained by Peter in the same way. In like manner certainly the rest also exhibit those whom they have as transmitters of the apostolic seed, appointed by the apostles to the episcopate. Let the heretics invent something of this kind. For what is forbidden to them after blasphemy? But even if they invent it, they will make no progress. For their doctrine itself, compared with the apostolic doctrine, will declare from its diversity and contrariety that it is neither of any apostolic author nor of an apostolic man, because just as the apostles would not have taught different things among themselves, so also apostolic men would not have published things contrary to the apostles. Unless those who learned from the apostles preached otherwise. Therefore by this standard they will be tested by those churches which, although they bring forward no author of theirs from the apostles or apostolic men, as being much later, which indeed are being established daily, nevertheless, agreeing in the same faith, are counted no less apostolic because of the kinship of doctrine. Thus all heresies, challenged by our churches according to both standards, let them prove themselves apostolic in whatever way they think. But so far they neither are nor can prove what they are not, nor are they received into peace and communion by churches apostolic in any way, evidently because of the diversity of their mystery they are in no way apostolic.

choices.why: Refers to the time period when the apostles lived and taught; 'age' captures the temporal sense of aetas.

choices.english: let them unroll the order of their bishops
choices.why: Evolvant literally means unroll (as a scroll), fitting the image of producing written records of succession.
Tradux means a vine-layer or offshoot; 'transmitters' preserves the idea of passing on the apostolic line.

choices.english: because of the kinship of doctrine
choices.why: Consanguinitas literally means blood-relationship; 'kinship' preserves the familial metaphor for doctrinal descent.
rejected: because of the close relationship of doctrine

choices.english: because of the diversity of their mystery
choices.why: Sacramentum here refers to the heretics' distinctive religious teaching or mystery; 'mystery' preserves the technical sense.
rejected: because of the difference of their sacrament
on account of the diversity of their sacred rite

pass_b_english: But suppose some of them dare to insert themselves into the apostolic age, so that they may seem to have been handed down by the apostles because they existed under the apostles. We can say to them: Let them produce the origins of their churches. Let them unroll the order of their bishops, running down from the beginning by succession in such a way that their first bishop had as his author and predecessor one of the apostles or apostolic men who nevertheless persevered with the apostles.

For this is how the apostolic churches present their records. The church of Smyrna reports that Polycarp was placed there by John. The church of Rome reports that Clement was ordained by Peter in the same way. Likewise the other churches certainly exhibit those whom they have as transmitters of the apostolic seed, appointed to the episcopate by the apostles.

Let the heretics invent something of this kind. For what is forbidden to them after blasphemy? But even if they invent it, they will gain nothing. For their doctrine itself, when compared with the apostolic doctrine, will declare by its diversity and contrariety that it has neither any apostle nor any apostolic man as its author. Just as the apostles would not have taught things different from one another, so apostolic men would not have published things contrary to the apostles—unless those who learned from the apostles preached otherwise.

By this standard, then, they will be tested by those churches which, although they can produce no apostle or apostolic man as their author, being much later and indeed being established daily, nevertheless are counted as no less apostolic because of the kinship of doctrine, since they agree in the same faith.

So all heresies, challenged by our churches according to both standards, must prove themselves apostolic in whatever way they think they are. But they are so far from being apostolic, and so unable to prove what they are not, that they are not received into peace and communion by churches that are apostolic in any way—clearly because of the diversity of their mystery, they are in no way apostolic.

polish.changed: Clarified the speaker and addressees, identified Polycarp as bishop of Smyrna and Clement as bishop of Rome, broke long sentences into natural modern units, and smoothed the flow for reading aloud while preserving every claim and qualification.

notes.why: Which Clement is not specified; reader may confuse him with other Clements.

notes.quote: Polycarp was placed there by John
notes.why: Polycarp is not identified; reader needs to know he was a bishop of Smyrna.
